title: Carbon intensity (CO2 emissions per dollar of GDP), 1820-2014
claim_summary: Surrounding chapter text discusses decarbonization, carbon intensity, and the claim that rich countries can reduce carbon emissions per dollar of GDP after industrialization.
book_citation: Ritchie & Roser 2017, based on data from CDIAC; GDP in 2011 international dollars with pre-1990 GDP from Maddison Project 2014.
original_dataset: OWID datasets: Carbon intensity (kgCO2/$) - Madisson, World Bank, CDIAC
notes: Minor typography and label-placement differences remain.; Current OWID successor data revise historical values substantially, so only post-2014 dashed segments are used in the extension.

title: CO2 emissions, 1960-2015
claim_summary: Surrounding chapter text argues that global emissions plateaued around 2014-2015, with changes in China, the EU, and the United States.
book_citation: Our World in Data, Ritchie & Roser 2017, the OWID annual CO2 emissions by region grapher, CDIAC, and Le Quere et al. 2016; international air and sea corresponds to bunker fuels, and Other corresponds to statistical difference.
original_dataset: OWID datasets: CO2 per year by region - CDIAC (2017)
notes: Layer labels and font styling are approximate.; Post-2015 extension uses current GCB/OWID successor categories, including EU-27 instead of EU-28 and no directly comparable statistical-difference layer.
